one_liner: Memory-safe Rust AV1 decoder (rav1d fork); faster only than upstream rav1d with its assembly disabled, slower than dav1d.
what_it_does: Fork of memorysafety/rav1d (itself a Rust port of dav1d) that decodes AV1 (8/10/12-bit, I400 to I444, film grain, HDR metadata) under crate-wide forbid(unsafe_code). All hand-written assembly is replaced by safe Rust SIMD. The native Rust API is Decoder::new()/with_settings(Settings), decode(&[u8]) returning Option<Frame>, and flush(), with zero-copy PlaneView8/PlaneView16 plane views, a Strictness policy and cooperative cancellation through Decoder::set_stop. Input must be raw OBU data (strip IVF/WebM framing, or use zenavif for AVIF) and output is planar YUV only. The optional c-ffi feature exports dav1d_* C symbols but lifts the unsafe-code ban.
how_it_is_fast: Against upstream's no-assembly build, the speed comes from having SIMD at all. rav1d-safe ports dav1d's x86 and ARM assembly families to safe Rust SIMD: motion compensation, inverse transforms, intra prediction, CDEF, loop filter, loop restoration, film grain, palette and refmvs, plus an inlined msac entropy decoder. It uses archmage capability-token dispatch (AVX2, some AVX-512, NEON) and safe_unaligned_simd loads. Upstream rav1d with default-features=false falls back to its scalar Rust code. Runtime DisjointMut overlap tracking stays on in the default build; on 4K AVIF it costs about 3.9 of 42.4 ms per frame against dav1d 1.5.3 (docs/SAFE_VS_DAV1D.md).
when_to_use: Decoding untrusted AVIF/AV1 stills in a Rust server where a forbid(unsafe_code) decoder with no assembly is a hard requirement
As a replacement for upstream rav1d built without assembly (for example, a target or policy that rules out nasm/asm): on 2K-8K photo stills it took 0.51-0.78x the time, and on map stills 0.755-1.002x
Tiled stills decoded with tile threading (1/4/8 workers, max_frame_delay=1), which works in the default checked build
Verifying AV1 encoder output: the default Strictness::Strict reports desynchronised symbol streams as errors where dav1d would conceal them
Cargo-only builds that still need SIMD on x86-64 (AVX2/AVX-512) and aarch64 (NEON)
when_not_to_use: When throughput is what matters: dav1d and default (assembly) rav1d are faster. The author's 2026-10-01 profile puts the default build at 1.72-1.74x dav1d 1.5.3's time on 4K stills, and the 2026-09-07 grid at 1.8-8.6x upstream's time (up to 12.8x against upstream frame threading)

Inter-heavy video playback: on a 480p inter stream the default build took 2.68 ms/frame against dav1d's 0.83, mostly in warp motion compensation, and frame threading in 0.6.0 needs the unchecked feature
Closed-source products without buying Imazen's commercial licence: the crate is AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Imazen-Commercial (the code inherited from dav1d/rav1d is BSD-2-Clause)
Pre-AVX2 x86 (no SSE tier, so it falls back to scalar) or ARM cores where dav1d's SVE2/dotprod/i8mm paths matter (only baseline NEON is ported)
Streams that need S-frames, SVC operating-point selection or the argon vectors: 19 of 803 dav1d-test-data vectors are not exercised

integration.dependencies: archmage, safe_unaligned_simd, rav1d-disjoint-mut, enough, whereat, parking_lot, zerocopy, strum, atomig, bitflags, raw-cpuid, aligned and small helpers; build dependencies cc and nasm-rs (assembly is used only by the opt-in asm/partial_asm modes); libc only with c-ffi
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (edition 2024); the AVIF test and benchmark tooling needs Rust 1.93
integration.platforms: x86-64 (AVX2 and partial AVX-512 SIMD; scalar below AVX2), aarch64 (NEON); i686, armv7 and riscv64gc listed as supported targets
integration.thread_safety: Internal tile-thread pool set by Settings.threads; Frame is Arc-backed and cloneable; Send/Sync for Decoder not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the native Rust API differs from upstream rav1d's Decoder/Picture API (decode(&[u8]) vs send_data/get_picture); the c-ffi/dav1d-compat features export dav1d_* C symbols but disable forbid(unsafe_code)

gotchas: Strictness::Strict is the default and rejects non-conforming streams that dav1d conceals; set Strictness::Lenient for dav1d-identical behaviour on corrupt input

Feature names moved after 0.6.0: the published crate's unchecked feature (frame threading, no overlap tracking) is called untracked on main, which also adds frame threading to tracked builds. The README table still says unchecked
Published 0.6.0 returns wrong mastering-display values (wrong fixed-point units; a 1000-nit maximum reads as 25.6 nits). The fix is only on main (Unreleased)
frame_size_limit defaults to 120 megapixels and bounds only declared dimensions, not decode time; use set_stop for cancellation on untrusted input
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick dav1d (catalogued, BSD-2-Clause, beats libaom) whenever speed or permissive licensing matters. Pick rav1d-safe only when a Rust decoder with no assembly and forbid(unsafe_code) is required. rusty-av1-toolkit is catalogued for its rav1e encoder speed; its rav1d-derived decoder has no catalogued decoder benchmark.
verified_claims_summary: On an AMD Ryzen 9 7900X with Rust 1.98.1 (LLVM 22.1.8), fat LTO, one codegen unit and identical RUSTFLAGS for both arms, checked rav1d-safe (commit be5b244, staged 0.6.0 with a git-pinned archmage, not the crates.io package that depends on archmage ^0.9.29) decoded 12 single-frame 8-bit 4:2:0 IVF stills in 0.680x (1 worker), 0.821x (4) and 0.813x (8) the time of upstream rav1d d3d1cd6 built with default-features=false. The stills are photo and map at 2K/4K/8K, each with minimum and eight tiles. Figures are geometric means of medians of five paired repetitions, and every run was MD5-checked against upstream and dav1d 1.5.3. The baseline is a non-default scalar build, and compare.py's rotate-then-reverse ordering cancels out for two arms, so upstream always ran first in each pair (the page discloses the fixed order).
status_note: Very active (commits on 2026-10-01; 0.6.0 published 2026-09-08 with about 15k total downloads; 451 closed issues, none open), but AGPL-3.0-only or a paid commercial licence and a speed deficit against dav1d make it a memory-safety pick, not a speed upgrade.
